maria: Heads-up — saw another burst of XID/ECC alerts in us-west2 last night that triggered ~12 node drains. noisy cards again :grimacing:
raj: Ugh. Any correlation with batch job churn or kernel updates?
taylor: I pulled the DCGM export timeline — lots of short-lived spikes on dcgm_gpu_ecc_errors_total and dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total, but mostly <1m each. Our current rule `for: 5m` still fires because of cumulative increase across the interval.
maria: Right. The rule is too sensitive to microbursts. Ops had to replace 3 cards unnecessarily. Can we try a windowed evaluation that ignores single short blips but still catches sustained degradation?
samir: Proposal: use a sliding window with weighted decay and require sustained rate increase + card-level streak. e.g. increase over 30m but also require sum_over_time(xid[10m:1m]) > threshold to prevent single-sample noise.
lee: Sketch of a rule I tested locally — it reduced false positives on my lab rack:

```yaml
- alert: GPU_Card_Flaky
  expr: |
    (
      sum by (gpu_uuid) (increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total[30m])) > 0
    )
    and
    (
      sum by (gpu_uuid) (increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total[10m])) > 2
    )
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "gpu {{ $labels.gpu_uuid }} exhibiting repeated XID spikes"
```

lee: Key difference: two-window check + short `for` to avoid immediate automation on single transient spikes.
raj: That looks promising. Would prefer a decayed scoring approach where older spikes matter less. We could compute a rolling score: score = sum(increase(...)[5m])*w0 + sum(increase(...)[10m])*w1 etc and alert when score > X.
maria: Also need playbook changes — don't auto-drain unless alert persists AND node-level health shows degraded throughput or ECC count rising across multiple GPUs. Drains in peak capacity zones cause capacity penalties.
taylor: Agreed. We should also route these alerts to a special channel with a `manual-review` receiver in Alertmanager, not auto-escalate to P1. Missed drains hurt SLAs/cost.
samir: For validation plan: 1) add new rules to staging cluster but disabled in production 2) run promtool test rules with synthetic series (I can generate noise + sustained faults) 3) enable in canary region (eu-central) for 48h 4) monitor suppressed counts and manual review hits
maria: @deploy-bot can we get a dry-run patch applied to staging? Add `team=eng-infra` label to make it easy to filter.
deploy-bot: (bot) I can apply the change to `prometheus-staging` namespace as a dry-run. Need a PR and the rule file.
raj: I'll draft a PR with two variants: `windowed-dual-check` and `decay-score` so we can A/B. Will include promtool tests and Grafana panels for the score.
lee: FYI — also add a small bump in alert cooldown in alertmanager routing for `gpu_*` alerts and switch `severity: warning` for the new rule.
taylor: One more operational safety: if alert leads to drain, check remaining free capacity in region; if <10% reserved capacity then block auto-drain and notify infra oncall to approve. Saves us from cascading capacity loss.
maria: Love it. Next steps: raj PR by EOD, samir will prepare synthetic test data, taylor will update routing proposal, lee will run local promtool sanitization. I'll coordinate canary. :thumbsup:
raj: On it.
samir: I'll drop the synthetic dataset and test results in the PR.
infra-bot: (bot) Created issue INFRA-4237: "Windowed DCGM alert rule + manual-review routing" and assigned to raj, samir, taylor, lee.
deploy-bot: (bot) Dry-run apply scheduled for `prometheus-staging` after PR merge.
lee: Quick note — keep `dcgm_gpu_memory_err_total` in mind too, similar noise patterns. We should reuse the same rule template.
maria: Good catch. We'll generalize the pattern. Thanks all.
raj: I'll ping this thread when PR is ready.
maria: Thanks — will follow the canary metrics closely. :eyes:
